about: The Trellis feature list. Work on the task that `scripts/tasks.py next` names. Tasks are never removed or reworded; only `passes` changes, through `scripts/tasks.py pass` after `scripts/tasks.py verify` succeeds. New tasks are appended with `scripts/tasks.py add`. Tasks with "review": "owner" also need the repository owner's sign-off, recorded in docs/PROGRESS.md.

tasks.title: Build, test and check scaffold
tasks.description: Create the CMake project, presets, warning and sanitizer setup, GoogleTest wiring, the compile-fail and golden-diagnostics runners, the developer scripts and the formatting and lint configuration that every later task relies on. The library stays empty apart from version and feature-detection headers. Verified preset, pre-commit, clang-tidy and GoogleTest snippets are in research/research_notes/Claude Code implementation practices/tooling_and_graphify.md.
acceptance: An INTERFACE target trellis::trellis with install rules and a CMake package config; a consumer project in tests/package/ builds against an installed copy with find_package(trellis CONFIG REQUIRED).

CMakePresets.json with configure, build and test presets gcc-13-debug, gcc-14-debug, clang-18-debug, clang-20-debug, clang-18-libcxx-debug, gcc-13-release, clang-18-release, asan-ubsan (clang-18), tsan (clang-18) and timetrace (clang-18 with -ftime-trace, no ccache): Ninja generator, build directories build/<preset>, CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON, ccache as compiler launcher when it is installed (never for timing builds).

The project warning set is applied to all project targets as errors. GCC and Clang: -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -Wnon-virtual-dtor -Wold-style-cast -Woverloaded-virtual. MSVC: /W4 /WX /permissive-.

include/trellis/trellis.hpp and include/trellis/config.hpp define TRELLIS_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH and TRELLIS_VERSION, plus TRELLIS_HAS_STATIC_ASSERT_MESSAGE, TRELLIS_HAS_EXPECTED, TRELLIS_HAS_PACK_INDEXING and TRELLIS_HAS_REFLECTION derived from standard feature-test macros. Unit tests cover them, and a generated test checks that every public header compiles on its own.
tests/unit uses GoogleTest and gMock (find_package(GTest) first, FetchContent fallback pinned to a release tag) with a smoke test registered through gtest_discover_tests.

tools/compile_fail.py, registered with CTest under the label compile_fail, compiles each tests/compile_fail/**/*.cpp with the preset's compiler and flags. Header directives: `// compile-fail: <summary>`, `// expect-id: <TRL-E...>` (optional), `// expect-regex: <regex>` (repeatable), `// expect-max-lines: <n>` (default 60). A test passes only when compilation fails and every expectation holds. Include a sample test, and a self-test proving that a file which compiles is reported as a failure.

tools/golden.py, registered with CTest under the label golden, normalizes compiler output (repo-relative paths; no line or column numbers, colors or version banners) and compares it with tests/diagnostics_golden/<compiler>-<major>/<name>.txt. `--update --reason "<why>"` rewrites goldens and appends the reason to docs/golden-changes.md. Include one sample golden.

Scripts: init.sh (check tools, configure and build clang-18-debug, run ctest); check-fast.sh (clang-format check of changed files, clang-18-debug build, ctest); check-full.sh (every local preset including sanitizers, at most 2 parallel jobs); tidy.sh (clang-tidy-18 on the given files, or on changed lines through clang-tidy-diff). Each prints a short summary (pass/fail counts and the first error of each failing step) and writes full logs to build/logs/.
.clang-format, .clang-tidy and .editorconfig; LICENSE with the official Boost Software License 1.0 text; a short CONTRIBUTING.md; CLAUDE.md's command list corrected if any command differs.
verify: cmake --install build/clang-18-debug --prefix build/install-test && cmake -S tests/package -B build/package-test -G Ninja -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$PWD/build/install-test && cmake --build build/package-test

tasks.title: CI workflows
tasks.description: GitHub Actions workflows that mirror the local scripts. The repository is private, so Actions minutes are limited: Linux runs on every push and pull request, and the heavier and non-Linux jobs run on a schedule and on demand.
acceptance: .github/workflows/ci.yml (push and pull_request): Linux jobs for gcc-13, gcc-14, clang-18, clang-20, clang-18-libcxx and asan-ubsan using the CMake presets, running the unit, compile_fail and golden tests; a ccache cache per preset; a concurrency group that cancels superseded runs.
.github/workflows/nightly.yml (daily schedule and workflow_dispatch): tsan and the quick compile-time benchmark on Linux.
.github/workflows/platforms.yml (weekly schedule and workflow_dispatch): configure, build and test on macOS (Apple Clang) and Windows (latest MSVC with Ninja).
scripts/ci-status.sh summarizes the latest runs with gh and prints the first errors of failed jobs (gh run view --log-failed).
The workflows pass actionlint. If actionlint cannot be installed in this environment, say so in docs/PROGRESS.md.
After pushing, the first ci.yml run is green, checked with scripts/ci-status.sh.

tasks.title: Benchmark harness and equivalence oracle
tasks.description: Port the research harness (research/experiments) into benchmarks/: generated dependency graphs for compile-time measurements, a runtime microbenchmark baseline, the budgets, and a generator that emits hand-wired programs with an identity checksum, so that later tasks can check Trellis against hand-written wiring.
acceptance: benchmarks/compile/gen_graph.py generates deterministic graphs of N components (fan-in 1 to 3, and 10) from a seed, emits a hand-wired program, and has an extension point for a trellis variant.

benchmarks/compile/run.py compiles generated programs one at a time with a timeout and a memory cap, never through ccache, records median wall time, peak RSS, and object and stripped binary sizes as JSON under build/bench/, and prints a table.
benchmarks/compile/budgets.json holds the NFR-03, NFR-04 and NFR-05 targets from plan §3.2 as ratios against hand-wiring.
benchmarks/runtime/ contains a Google Benchmark program for the research scenario (resolve the root, build the graph), wired by hand.
tests/property/ checks sharing semantics of random hand-wired graphs through a checksum (CTest label property). CI uses seeds that local runs do not.
scripts/bench-compile.sh [--quick] (quick: N = 10, 50 and 100 with gcc-13 and clang-18) and scripts/bench-runtime.sh.

tasks.title: Spike S1: deduced constructor discovery
tasks.description: Find the set of conversion operators for placeholder arguments that resolves every constructor-parameter form without ambiguity, measure the cost of arity probing, and document the limits. Use the /spike skill.
acceptance: spikes/S1-deduced-discovery/ contains the prototype header, the test programs, and run.sh, which reproduces every result on gcc-13, gcc-14, clang-18, clang-20 and clang-18 with libc++.

docs/spikes/S1-deduced-discovery.md has a table of at least 12 parameter forms by compiler (T, T&, const T&, T&&, T*, const T*, unique_ptr<T>, shared_ptr<T>, const shared_ptr<T>&, std::function, std::span, std::optional, plus any others found relevant). Every cell is either resolved or explained.
Arity probing cost is measured: compile time for 100 classes with 0 to 8 parameters.

Each limit has a detection strategy and an intended error: constructor templates, variadic constructors, same-arity overloads, defaulted parameters, aggregates, private or deleted constructors, abstract types.
Includes an MSVC risk assessment (MSVC cannot be tested here) and a recommendation that confirms or amends ADR-03.

tasks.title: Spike S3: diagnostics rendering
tasks.description: Prototype how Trellis reports wiring errors in C++20 (a static_assert whose condition names an error type) and in C++26 (user-generated static_assert messages), and measure what each compiler prints. Use the /spike skill.
acceptance: spikes/S3-diagnostics/ prototypes E001, E005 and E012, each at the root and three levels deep, with run.sh reproducing everything on gcc-13, gcc-14, clang-18 and clang-20. C++26 message forms are tested with clang -std=c++2c and gcc-14 -std=c++26.
docs/spikes/S3-diagnostics.md records, per compiler and form: the first error line, total lines and bytes, and whether errors cascade, together with the technique used to stop cascades.
Shows constexpr type names from __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ on GCC and Clang, and the normalization rules for golden tests.
Compares against the Boost.DI and Fruit outputs in research/experiments/results/logs/diagnostics.
Gives a recommendation for ADR-06 and a verdict on whether the 40-line budget is feasible.

tasks.title: Spike S4: storage and threading
tasks.description: Choose the design of lazily initialized singleton slots and of the teardown stack by measurement. Use the /spike skill.
acceptance: spikes/S4-storage-threading/ compares std::call_once per slot with an atomic state machine: slot size, warm and cold access cost, and contention with 8 threads (Google Benchmark), with run.sh.
Covers retry after an exception during construction, re-entrancy detection (R004), teardown order, and shared_ptr versus inline storage.
ThreadSanitizer is clean on the stress tests.
docs/spikes/S4-storage-threading.md recommends a design for ADR-12 and §7.6.

tasks.title: Spike S2: memoization and cycles
tasks.description: Measure how resolution strategies scale at compile time and decide how deduced mode handles dependency cycles. Build on S1's prototype and T0.3's graph generator. Use the /spike skill.
acceptance: spikes/S2-memoization-cycles/ compares per-key memoization, depth-bounded and path-tracked variants at N = 25, 50, 100 and 250 (500 and 1000 if within the memory caps), with fan-in 3 and 10, on gcc-13 and clang-18. run.sh supports --quick.
Measures instantiation depth per dependency hop with -ftemplate-depth sweeps on chains of 50 to 500.
Records what each compiler reports for a cycle under each variant.
docs/spikes/S2-memoization-cycles.md recommends the cycle option for §7.3 and confirms or revises NFR-09.

tasks.title: Architecture decision records
tasks.description: Write one ADR per decision in plan §4, updated with the spike results.
acceptance: docs/adr/0001-*.md to 0013-*.md, one per ADR in plan §4. Each has a Status line plus Context, Decision, Alternatives and Consequences sections.
Spike outcomes are folded in. Decisions a spike changed are marked 'Accepted (provisional, awaiting owner review)' and listed in docs/PROGRESS.md.
Spikes S5 (reflection: needs GCC 16, which isn't packaged for Ubuntu 24.04) and S6 (runtime dependency recording: belongs to Phase 5) are recorded as deferred, with the reasons.

tasks.title: Meta toolkit
tasks.description: The compile-time utilities the engine is built on: type lists, an inheritance-based type map with duplicate detection, fixed strings, constexpr type names and the result type.
interfaces: trellis::detail::type_list<Ts...>; contains_v<T, List>; index_of_v<T, List>; at_t<I, List>
acceptance: Unit and static_assert tests cover every utility on all local presets.
type_name gives readable names on GCC and Clang for class, template, pointer and reference types.
No recursive variadic templates: algorithms use fold expressions, and lookups use overload resolution.
Headers are self-contained and warning-free (NFR-10).

tasks.title: Explicit constructor declaration
tasks.description: The explicit discovery strategy: a trait the user can specialize, an opt-in member alias, and a hook point for .with_ctor<Args...>().
acceptance: Both the specialization and the member alias work. When both are present, the specialization wins, as documented.
A declaration that doesn't match any constructor is a compile error with a clear message (compile-fail test).
Unit tests pass on all local presets.

tasks.title: Deduced constructor discovery
tasks.description: Automatic, macro-free constructor discovery using the placeholder-argument technique chosen in spike S1.
acceptance: any_arg follows S1's chosen set of conversion operators. Arity probing goes up to options.max_ctor_arity (default 16), excludes copy and move constructors, and handles aggregates.
Every limit found in S1 has a compile-fail test producing E004, E010 or the documented message.
Each parameter form in the S1 table has a resolution test, run on all local presets.

tasks.title: Binding vocabulary and modules
tasks.description: The binding vocabulary, lifetimes, modules and options, plus the request-form compatibility table.
acceptance: Duplicate keys across modules produce E003 (compile-fail test).
The request-form table in plan §6.3 is encoded as constexpr data with a test for each cell. E005 and E012 have compile-fail tests.
Modules are flattened once, and no fluent chain accumulates bindings in a type.

tasks.title: Storage, lifetimes and create<T>
tasks.description: Per-injector storage, teardown and object creation for every allowed request form. The research scenario is wired with Trellis end to end.
acceptance: Singleton slots are per injector (shared_ptr storage by default, inline as an option). Teardown runs in reverse order of construction, shown by recorded-destructor tests.
unique, external and value lifetimes work. create<T>() supports every request form the table allows, and identity tests check sharing.
The research scenario (research/experiments/common/domain.hpp) wired with Trellis compiles without warnings and behaves like the hand-wired version. ASan and UBSan are clean.

tasks.title: Diagnostics in C++20 form
tasks.description: Root-cause compile errors with stable IDs and the dependency path, rendered as S3 recommends.
acceptance: Error types exist for E001-E005, E009, E010 and E012. Exactly one static_assert fires per root cause, with no cascading errors.
A minimal explain pass reports the path from the root.
Every ID has a compile-fail test, and there are golden tests for gcc-13, gcc-14, clang-18 and clang-20.
NFR-07 holds: the first error line names the type and the ID, and output stays at or under 40 lines on GCC and Clang.

tasks.title: Test overrides and testing helpers
tasks.description: Overrides for tests, plus helpers to check that a graph can be wired.
acceptance: trellis::override<K> replaces an existing binding. With nothing to override, it is error E009 (compile-fail test).
trellis::testing::wireable<Injector, Root> and trellis::testing::create_all work.
A gMock example test exists, and a test shows that singletons are isolated per injector.

tasks.title: C++20 module and single header
tasks.description: Deliver the library as a C++20 module and as a generated single header, both tested.
acceptance: modules/trellis.cppm exports the public API. It builds and passes a smoke test with CMake 3.28 and Ninja on clang-18 and clang-20, and on gcc-14 if its module support is sufficient (otherwise documented).
tools/amalgamate.py produces single_include/trellis.hpp, a gitignored build artifact that passes the unit tests.

tasks.title: v0.1 benchmarks against budgets
tasks.description: Measure Trellis against hand-written wiring and the budgets, and check it against the equivalence oracle.
acceptance: There is a trellis variant in gen_graph.py and in the runtime benchmark.
The equivalence oracle passes on 200 random graphs (Trellis versus hand-wired checksums).
NFR-01, NFR-03, NFR-06, and a 100-component compile within 1.3x of hand-wiring, are measured on gcc-13 and clang-18 and recorded in docs/benchmarks/v0.1.md.
If a budget is missed, stop and report it. Never change budgets.json to make a result pass.

tasks.title: v0.1 release

acceptance: README has a quick start whose hello world (plan §6.1) compiles as a test. docs/getting-started.md and CHANGELOG.md exist.
A cleanup and simplification pass reports the core line count (NFR-12).
The /phase-gate 1 report is written to docs/gates/phase-1.md, and CI is green.
Tag v0.1.0 only after the owner approves.

tasks.title: Golden normalization (owner-approved)
tasks.description: Align tools/golden.py and the compile-fail runner's environment with spike S3's normalization rules, and normalize every path to '/'. This also fixes the Windows golden self-test. The owner approved this on 2026-10-30, including regenerating the sample golden through tools/golden.py --update and updating the MSVC self-test expectation.
acceptance: Normalization drops quoted source excerpts, caret lines, include chains, and the 'N errors generated.' and 'compilation terminated.' lines. It strips ANSI and OSC-8 escapes, maps typographic quotes to ', rewrites paths to <src>/ and <std>/ placeholders with '/' separators, and rewrites :line:col to :L:C.

tools/golden.py and tools/compile_fail.py run compilers with LC_ALL=C and a clean environment (no inherited CPATH, CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH, GCC_URLS or similar), with -fdiagnostics-plain-output on GCC and -fno-color-diagnostics -fno-caret-diagnostics on Clang.

The sample golden is regenerated with tools/golden.py --update, with the reason logged in docs/golden-changes.md. The tests/tools self-tests are updated to the new rules, including the MSVC case, which now expects '/'.
tools.golden_selftest passes on Windows in platforms.yml: dispatch a run on a work branch and check the result.
